topic: Strange borders: the Matterhorn border that moves, and more
hook: Your hike near the Matterhorn can cross a border that moves with the weather.
title: The Matterhorn Border Moves. 6 More Make No Sense
description:
Melting glaciers have moved the Swiss-Italian border near the Matterhorn, and the two countries agreed a new line. This countdown covers seven real borders that make no sense, from a Spanish town inside France to a village in India that was once land inside land inside land. Watch to the end for the strangest one.

#borders #geography #facts

scenes.narration: Your hike near the Matterhorn can cross a border that moves with the weather. Melting ice is literally shifting the line between two countries.
scenes.headline: A Border That Moves

scenes.narration: That is only one of seven real borders in this video that make no sense. And the last one is in India.
scenes.headline: 7 Real Borders

scenes.narration: By the end, you will see a piece of India that was land inside land inside land, inside another country.
scenes.headline: India's Strangest

scenes.narration: Each one is stranger than the one before it. So let's count down from seven.
scenes.headline: Counting Down

scenes.narration: Every place here is on a normal map. Nothing is made up, and you can look all of them up yourself.
scenes.headline: All On The Map

scenes.narration: Starting with a town that Spain owns, in the middle of France.
scenes.headline: Number 7

scenes.narration: Number seven. Llívia is a Spanish town, and France surrounds it on every side.
scenes.headline: Llívia

scenes.narration: In 1659, Spain and France signed a treaty and handed villages over to France.
scenes.headline: The Treaty

scenes.narration: But Llívia was officially a town, not a village. So the treaty skipped it, and it stayed Spanish.
scenes.headline: Town, Not Village

scenes.narration: Today you can stand in a Spanish town and see only French countryside around you.
scenes.headline: Spain In France

scenes.narration: A later treaty, in 1866, made a special road to connect Llívia to the rest of Spain.
scenes.headline: The Neutral Road

scenes.narration: It is called a neutral road. France cannot put a customs checkpoint on it.
scenes.headline: No Checkpoints

scenes.narration: So you drive from France, through a strip that belongs to nobody's rules, into a Spanish town.
scenes.headline: Drive Right In

scenes.narration: That is a strange map. But the next one has a village living by two sets of rules.
scenes.headline: Stranger Next

scenes.narration: Number six is a village that wanted to leave its own country.
scenes.headline: Number 6

scenes.narration: Büsingen is a German village, and Switzerland almost completely surrounds it.
scenes.headline: Büsingen

scenes.narration: In 1918, the villagers held their own vote about joining Switzerland. About 96 percent said yes.
scenes.headline: They Voted To Leave

scenes.narration: Switzerland said no, because Germany wanted too much money in exchange. So the village stayed German.
scenes.headline: Too Expensive

scenes.narration: Today it is politically part of Germany, but economically part of the Swiss customs area.
scenes.headline: Two Systems

scenes.narration: Shops there can take both euros and Swiss francs. Your wallet needs to be ready for two currencies.
scenes.headline: Two Currencies

scenes.narration: And that is a village that is German on paper but Swiss in daily life.
scenes.headline: German On Paper

scenes.narration: Now think about the opposite: a place that is Italian, but lives like Switzerland.
scenes.headline: The Opposite Case

scenes.narration: That is number five, and it has a casino as big as the town.
scenes.headline: Number 5

scenes.narration: Campione d'Italia is Italian land on the shore of Lake Lugano, inside Swiss territory.
scenes.headline: Campione d'Italia

scenes.narration: The euro is the legal currency, but people there use the Swiss franc in daily life.
scenes.headline: Swiss Francs

scenes.narration: Cars are registered with Swiss authorities, even though the town belongs to Italy.
scenes.headline: Swiss Number Plates

scenes.narration: And the casino there is a giant landmark, with gambling rules that are different from both countries.
scenes.headline: A Huge Casino

scenes.narration: So you can be in Italy and pay in Swiss money. But next, the border itself starts to move.
scenes.headline: Next: It Moves

scenes.narration: Number four is the one from the start. A border that melts.
scenes.headline: Number 4

scenes.narration: In the high Alps, the Swiss-Italian border does not follow a fence or a river.
scenes.headline: No Fence At All

scenes.narration: It follows the watershed, the crest line of snow and glaciers, where water flows one way or the other.
scenes.headline: The Ice Line

scenes.narration: But glaciers are melting. When the ice shrinks, the crest line moves, and so does the border.
scenes.headline: Melting Moves It

scenes.narration: If you like strange places and facts like this, a subscribe would help a lot. There are many more coming.
scenes.headline: Enjoying This?

scenes.narration: Near Zermatt in Switzerland and Breuil-Cervinia in Italy, the line is no longer where the old map put it.
scenes.headline: Zermatt And Cervinia

scenes.narration: So Switzerland and Italy agreed on a new border in 2023, and Switzerland approved it in 2024.
scenes.headline: A New Line

scenes.narration: Reports say Switzerland gains a little land, and the deal also covers mountain huts, like the Carrel refuge.
scenes.headline: Mountain Huts

scenes.narration: The huts matter, because climbers sleep there. The countries want each hut to stay in the country it is in now.
scenes.headline: Climbers' Beds

scenes.narration: That is a border written in ice, and the ice is disappearing. Next, a piece of America only reachable through Canada.
scenes.headline: Next: America

scenes.narration: Number three starts with a map mistake from long ago.
scenes.headline: Number 3

scenes.narration: The Northwest Angle is part of Minnesota, in the United States, but it sits north of the rest of the state.
scenes.headline: Northwest Angle

scenes.narration: Old treaty-makers worked from a map that was wrong about where the Mississippi River begins.
scenes.headline: A Map Error

scenes.narration: When the border was drawn, the mistake left a small piece of Minnesota attached to the wrong side.
scenes.headline: Left Over Land

scenes.narration: To drive there by road, you have to pass through Canada, in the province of Manitoba.
scenes.headline: Drive Through Canada

scenes.narration: Imagine going home in your own country, and needing to cross another country to do it.
scenes.headline: Home Via Canada

scenes.narration: It is a small corner of land and lakes, and it is still part of the United States.
scenes.headline: Still American

scenes.narration: That is a mistake on a map. Next is a whole region cut off from its own country.
scenes.headline: Next: A Region

scenes.narration: Number two is bigger than any town. It is a piece of Russia that Russia cannot reach by land.
scenes.headline: Number 2

scenes.narration: Kaliningrad sits on the Baltic Sea, with Poland on one side and Lithuania on the other.
scenes.headline: Between Two Countries

scenes.narration: Russia's main land is far to the east. So Kaliningrad is separated from it by other countries.
scenes.headline: Cut Off

scenes.narration: The city used to be called Königsberg, and it was German until 1945.
scenes.headline: It Was German

scenes.narration: After the Second World War, it became Russian. Today it is a Russian region inside the European Union's neighbourhood.
scenes.headline: Now Russian

scenes.narration: That is a big place that is cut off. But now we reach the one that India made even more complicated.
scenes.headline: Now, India

scenes.narration: Number one is in West Bengal, in the Cooch Behar area, along the India-Bangladesh border.
scenes.headline: Cooch Behar

scenes.narration: For decades, there were small patches of Indian land inside Bangladesh, and Bangladeshi land inside India.
scenes.headline: Land Inside Land

scenes.narration: These patches are called enclaves. There were more than 160 of them, all packed along one border.
scenes.headline: 160+ Enclaves

scenes.narration: Imagine living in a village that is Indian, but every road out of it leads into another country.
scenes.headline: Surrounded

scenes.narration: Residents often had trouble reaching schools, hospitals and officials, because the country around them was the other one.
scenes.headline: No Easy Services

scenes.narration: Then there was the strangest piece of all. It was called Dahala Khagrabari.
scenes.headline: The Strangest Piece

scenes.narration: It was Indian land, inside Bangladeshi land, inside Indian land, inside Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: Four Layers

scenes.narration: It was the only third-order enclave in the world. That means land inside land inside land, inside a country.
scenes.headline: World's Only One

scenes.narration: You could be standing on Indian soil and be three borders deep inside Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: Three Borders Deep

scenes.narration: The two countries agreed to fix this. At midnight on 31 July 2015, the enclaves were exchanged.
scenes.headline: Midnight Exchange

scenes.narration: India received 51 Bangladeshi enclaves. Bangladesh received 111 Indian enclaves.
scenes.headline: 51 And 111

scenes.narration: People living there could choose whether they wanted to live in India or in Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: They Could Choose

scenes.narration: For many, it meant they finally had a road, a school and a vote in the country they lived in.
scenes.headline: A Vote At Last

scenes.narration: So the strangest border of all was not a wall or a war zone. It was a puzzle of tiny islands of land.
scenes.headline: A Puzzle Of Land

scenes.narration: And most of that puzzle is gone now, solved by one midnight in 2015.
scenes.headline: Solved In 2015

scenes.narration: So that is seven borders. Spain inside France, and Germany inside Switzerland.
scenes.headline: Recap

scenes.narration: Italy using Swiss money, and a Matterhorn border that melts and moves.
scenes.headline: Recap

scenes.narration: A piece of Minnesota you reach through Canada, and a Russian region cut off from Russia.
scenes.headline: Recap

scenes.narration: And India's land inside land inside land, in Bengal. All real, and all on the map.
scenes.headline: India's Winner

scenes.narration: The Matterhorn one is still changing, because glaciers are still melting. The line you hiked on may not be the line next year.
scenes.headline: The Line Still Moves

scenes.narration: Your hike near the Matterhorn can cross a border that moves with the weather.
scenes.headline: It Moves

scenes.narration: Tomorrow: the country that has no border at its own front door.
scenes.headline: Tomorrow
